notes:
Council considered Dundee Secondary Plan – Official Plan Amendment OPA24/009/COK/CM and Class Environmental Assessment - Statutory Public Meeting, DSD-2026-205, and addendum report DSD-2026-244, listed as item 7.5.a on the agenda this date. Council was also in receipt of written submissions from John Alati, Davis Howe LLP, and Heather Price, GSP Group, on behalf of Schlegel Urban Development. Natalie Goss, Manager, Policy and Research and Rosa Bustamante, Director, Planning and Housing Policy/City Planner. 

It was noted since the May 25, 2026 Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee, staff had an opportunity to further review the received written submissions and have provided an addendum report, Development Services Department report DSD-2026-244, as a follow-up to the Committees questions. The report includes a revised recommendation for Councils consideration.

Pierre Chauvin, MHBC Planning, was in attendance to respond to questions from Council if required.

John Alati, Davis Howe LLP, addressed Council on behalf of Schlegel Urban Development, requesting the following changes to the Dundee Secondary Plan, including but not limited to: mapping and requested amendments to reflect commercial designation and that floor space ratio (FSR) allocations be amended to align with the special policy.

Councillor J. Deneault left and returned to the meeting.

Councillor M. Johnston left and returned to the meeting.

N. Goss, Manager, Policy and Research responded to questions from Council.

A motion was brought forward by Councillor P. Singh, which was seconded by Councillor D. Chapman to approve the recommendation as outlined in the Addendum Report DSD-2026-244.

Councillor S. Davey moved an amendment which was then seconded by Councillor C. Michaud "that policy 13.55 requiring a minimum floor space ratio, be removed" which was then voted on and Carried.

Councillor B. Ioannidis left the meeting at this time.

Councillor S. Stretch moved an amendment which was then seconded by Councillor D. Chapman "that Policy 5.6 be amended as follows: 5.6. Development for residential uses on sites of one hectare or more of developable lands should provide a minimum of 30 percent of new homes in forms other than single detached, semi-detached, and street fronting and single unit condominium townhouse units."

It was noted that further discussion on this matter would have implications on the approval of the item 7.6.d. Kitchener 2051 - New Official Plan, at the Direction of the Mayor, Council agreed to table this matter until the completion of that matter.

items.title: Kitchener 2051 - New Official Plan, DSD-2026-235, and addendum report DSD-2026-252, listed as item 7.6.d
notes:
Council considered Kitchener 2051 - New Official Plan, DSD-2026-235, and addendum report DSD-2026-252, listed as item 7.6.d on the agenda this date. Council was also in receipt of written submissions from Heather Price, GSP Group, on behalf of Schlegel Urban Development, Andrew Milne, Hal Jaeger, Melissa Bowman and Sam Nabi. Natalie Goss, Manager, Policy and Research and Rosa Bustamante, Director, Planning and Housing Policy/City Planner. 

It was noted since the June 1, 2026 Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee, staff had an opportunity to further review the received written submissions and have provided an addendum report, Development Services Department report DSD-2026-252, as a follow-up to the Committees questions. The report does include a revised recommendation for Councils consideration.

Pierre Chauvin, MHBC Planning, was in attendance in support of the staff recommendation and to respond to questions from Council if required.

Councillor S. Davey left and returned to the meeting at this time. 

Heather Mackay delegated in support of policy provision 11.SPA.46 with maximum height of 3 stories in the Auditorium area and the amendment approved by the Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee. 

Councillor J. Deneault left and returned the meeting at this time.

Heather Price, GSP Group, on behalf of Schlegel Urban Development delegated in opposition with respect to three policy issues, Food Store provisions for two properties owned by Schlegel, remaining existing land use entitlements and what they perceive to be "down zoning" and sought site specific exemptions to permit uses, and acceptance of legal non-conforming uses to permit drive thru locations where they will be prohibited.

Melissa Bowman, delegated in opposition of the recommendation to two neighbourhood exemptions removed through amendment at the Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee to reduce height restrictions in the Westmount and Auditorium areas and requested Council approve the Official Plan as originally recommended by staff. 

Andrew Milne delegated in support of protecting institutional lands within Protected Major Transit Station Areas (PMTSA) to ensure that institutional lands can be retained and requested that amendments to policy be made.

Councillor M. Johnston left and returned to the meeting at this time. 

Hal Jaeger delegated in support of amending policies 3.9 and 2.38 so that freehold home ownership is maintained, noting mis-alignment between policy 3.9 with the Region of Waterloo Official Plan Amendment #6. H. Jaeger recommended two policy amendments related to 3.6 and 2.38. H. Jaeger then responded to questions from Council. 

Councillor S. Stretch left and returned to the meeting at this time. 

Michael Witmer, delegated in support of the overall direction however expressed concern with the Mixed Use B designation and commercial plaza recognition as a Strategic Growth Area (SGA) area and restrictions on drive thru facilities which will impact his property at 563 Highland Road. M. Witmer requested the site specific policy framework in the first and second draft be adopted such that  existing drive thru facilities can continue to operate future drive thru facilities not require a separate zoning by-law amendment (ZBA). M. Witmer then responded to questions from Council.

items.title: Kitchener 2051 - New Official Plan, DSD-2026-235, and addendum report DSD-2026-252, listed as item 7.6.d (Cont'd)
notes:
Council resumed consideration of Kitchener 2051 - New Official Plan, DSD-2026-235, and addendum report DSD-2026-252, listed as item 7.6.d on the agenda this date.

J. Readman, General Manager, Development Services, then addressed Council with respect to the amendments.

Councillor D. Chapman brought forward a motion to approve the recommendation as outlined in Addendum report DSD-2026-252, which was seconded by Councillor S. Davey.

Councillor D. Chapman brought forward an amendment, which was seconded by Councillor S. Stretch to amend Policy 3.9 be amended as follows: “Notwithstanding policy 3.9, development for residential uses on sites of two hectares or more of developable lands, should provide a minimum of 60 percent of new homes in forms other than single detached, and semi-detached dwellings, and street fronting and single unit condominium townhouse units; and, to amend Policy 2.38 be amended as follows: Development on lands outside of Built-up Area (developed as of June 16, 2006) will be planned to achieve a minimum density of 133 residents and jobs per hectare by 2051. Vacant Lands not subject to draft approved Plans of Subdivision as of December 31, 2025, will be cumulatively planned to a minimum density of 133 residents and jobs per hectare.”

Councillor D. Chapman's amendment related to Policy 3.9, was then voted on and was LOST.

Councilor D. Chapman's amendment related to Policy 2.38, was then voted on and was LOST.

Councillor S. Stretch brought forward an amendment, which was seconded by Councillor D. Chapman, to amend Policy 3.9 as follows: Development for residential uses on sites of one hectare or more of developable lands should provide a minimum of 30 percent of new homes in forms other than single detached, semi-detached, and street fronting and single unit condominium townhouse units.”

Councillor Stretch's amendment was then voted on and was LOST.

Councillor S. Davey brought forward an amendment, which was seconded by Councillor B. Ioannidis, as follows: 

"That City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/002/COK/JZ, for the purpose of implementing anew Official Plan for the City of Kitchener, be adopted, in the form shown in the Official Plan Amendment attached to Report DSD-2026-235 as Attachment ‘A’ and amended as follows, and accordingly forwarded to the Province of Ontario for approval; and,

1.  That a site specific policy be added to 1950 Fischer-Hallman Road as follows:
            a)    Notwithstanding the Mixed Use B land use designation and policy 11.47, on lands municipally known as 1950 Fischer-Hallman Road the following                     uses will also be permitted:
                       i.    Drive-through facilities. 

2.  That a site specific policy be added to 1415 Huron Road as follows:
            a)    Notwithstanding the Mixed Use B land use designation and policy 11.47, on lands municipally known as 1950 Fischer-Hallman Road the following                     uses will also be permitted:
                       i.    Drive-through facilities. 

3.    That a site specific policy be added to 1187 Fischer-Hallman Road as follows:
            a)    Notwithstanding the Mixed Use B land use designation, including policy 11.47, on land municipally known as 1187 Fischer-Hallman Road the                           following uses will also be permitted:
                          i.    Drive-through facilities;
                          ii.    Gas stations;
                          iii.    Car washes; and
                          iv.    Repair of motor vehicles.

4.    That a site specific policy be added to 1111 Westmount Road East, 1170, 1178, 1188 and 1191 Fischer-Hallman Road as follows:
            a)    Notwithstanding the Mixed Use A and Mixed Use B land use, including policies 11.36 and 11.47, on land municipally known as 1111 Westmount                       Road East, 1170, 1178, 1188 and 1191 Fischer-Hallman Road the following uses will also be permitted:
                           i.    Drive-through facilities;
                           ii.    Gas stations;
                           iii.    Car washes; and
                           iv.    Repair of motor vehicles; and,

That City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/002/COK/JZ, for the purpose of implementing a new Official Plan for the City of Kitchener, be adopted, in the form shown in the Official Plan Amendment attached to Report DSD-2026-235 as Attachment ‘A’ and amended as follows, and accordingly forwarded to the Province of Ontario for approval; and further,  

That 585 Bridgeport Road be designated “Commercial First” on Map 3 Land Use and that a new site specific provision be added to this portion of the property not permitting residential uses."

Councillor S. Davey's amendment was then voted on and was Carried.

Councillor B. Ioannidis then brought forward an amendment to revise Policy 7.155.m of the draft Official Plan to remove ‘heritage corridors’ and ‘trails’ from the list of exclusions for parkland dedication. Councillor B. Ioannidis amendment was LOST, as it failed to receive a seconder.

Councillor A. Owodunni left the meeting at this time.

Councillor M. Johnston then brought forward an amendment, which was seconded by Councillor C. Michaud, as follows: 

"That a site specific policy be added to 491, 525, and 536 Highland Road West,  as follows:
1.    Notwithstanding the Mixed Use B land use designation and policy 11.47, on lands municipally known as 491, 525, and 536 Highland Road West the following uses will also be permitted:
               i. Drive-through facilities." 

Councillor M. Johnston's amendment was voted on and was Carried.

Councillor D. Chapman then brought forward a further amendment, as follows: "That staff be directed to further study institutional land uses, including lands within the protected major transit station areas, and have conversations with institutional land users to understand how to best maintain social infrastructure needs through land use planning instruments now and into the future and report back by Q2 2027." 

In response to feedback from staff on Councillor Chapmans amendment related to institutional lands, Mayor B. Vrbanovic noted the matter was not germane to the decision of Council this date and requested any motions related to institutional land uses be brought back to Council through a Notice of Motion at a future Council meeting.

Councillor P. Singh left and re-entered the meeting at this time.

As per the previously declared conflict by Councillor P. Singh, the  Strategic Growth Area Designations in the Highland Road-Belmont Street, Connaught Street-Franklin Street South and the Stirling Street-Mill Street vicinities, were then voted and were Carried.

The balance of the Official Plan, as amended was then voted on.

motions.item_title: Notice of Motion - P. Singh - Pothole Technology Exploration
motions.text: "WHEREAS the past two winter seasons presented unusually challenging conditions for roadway maintenance, resulting in increased pothole formation due to prolonged deep freezes, significant temperature fluctuations and significant spring rainfall; and, WHEREAS Council has expressed ongoing interest in improving roadway condition monitoring and ensuring timely, efficient repair of potholes; and, WHEREAS staff have been actively working to strengthen data collection methodologies to better track road conditions and inform operational decision-making; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT staff be directed to explore opportunities to enhance the City’s pothole monitoring and repair program, including: a. Improvements to data collection, tracking, and reporting tools using AI technology to provide more accurate and timely information on roadway conditions; b. Options to optimize resource allocation and response times for pothole repair, taking into consideration service demand and operational constraints; and, c. Using data to inform long-term approach to roadway maintenance and asset management, including service level expectations and funding strategies; and, THEREFORE BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that staff report back with findings and recommendations through a future budget discussion."
motions.text_html:
"WHEREAS the past two winter seasons presented unusually challenging conditions for roadway maintenance, resulting in increased pothole formation due to prolonged deep freezes, significant temperature fluctuations and significant spring rainfall; and,

WHEREAS Council has expressed ongoing interest in improving roadway condition monitoring and ensuring timely, efficient repair of potholes; and,

WHEREAS staff have been actively working to strengthen data collection methodologies to better track road conditions and inform operational decision-making;

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT staff be directed to explore opportunities to enhance the City’s pothole monitoring and repair program, including:

a. Improvements to data collection, tracking, and reporting tools using AI technology to provide more accurate and timely information on roadway conditions;

b. Options to optimize resource allocation and response times for pothole repair, taking into consideration service demand and operational constraints; and,

c. Using data to inform long-term approach to roadway maintenance and asset management, including service level expectations and funding strategies; and,

THEREFORE BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that staff report back with findings and recommendations through a future budget discussion."
